options.name: Bulletproof Machinery
options.summary: Mechanical DNFs are almost unheard of with a 0.06% per-lap failure chance.
options.description: Suppliers and teams focus on bulletproof components, dramatically cutting unexpected DNFs.

options.name: High Reliability
options.summary: Baseline 0.10% per-lap mechanical failure chance remains in force.
options.description: The governing body keeps reliability expectations steady, matching the series' modern attrition rates.

options.name: Good Reliability
options.summary: Teams face a 0.20% per-lap mechanical failure chance.
options.description: Cost saving measures loosen component quality targets slightly, nudging the grid toward modest attrition.

options.name: Meddling Reliability
options.summary: Mechanical trouble creeps up to a 0.30% per-lap failure chance.
options.description: Rule tweaks disrupt team supply chains, increasing the odds of a mechanical drama on Sundays.

options.name: Bad Reliability
options.summary: Reliability nosedives to a 0.45% per-lap mechanical failure chance.
options.description: Harsh component limits and budget clamps spark an attrition-heavy era packed with breakdowns.

minor.name: Minor
minor.summary: A mild technical refresh trims carryover only slightly.

major.name: Major
major.summary: A meaningful regulation shift compresses the field and rewards the right concept call.

drastic.name: Drastic
drastic.summary: A major reset heavily compresses carryover and magnifies concept fit.

options.name: Balanced Era
options.summary: Neutral technical rules leave concept strengths largely untouched.
options.description: The rulebook remains balanced enough that no chassis concept receives an external bonus or penalty.

options.name: High Downforce Era
options.summary: High-downforce concepts gain extra value while slippery, conservative ideas lose some edge.
options.description: The rules reward cars that generate strong medium-speed load and robust wake control, punishing flatter or conservative solutions.

options.name: Low-Drag Era
options.summary: Low-drag concepts gain extra value while higher-downforce solutions become less rewarding.
options.description: Simplified aero surfaces and drag trims reward efficient top-end concepts, while high-downforce and wake-heavy solutions lose ground.

options.name: Conservative Packaging Era
options.summary: Stable, robust packaging concepts gain value while aggressive brake-duct ideas lose some edge.
options.description: The rules favor reliable, clean-flow packaging and penalize concepts that rely heavily on aggressive brake-duct and low-speed aero shaping.

options.name: Stability-Assisted Era
options.summary: Cornering and braking skill translate to the usual 0.05s per point.
options.description: Electronics and chassis setup aid the drivers just enough to mirror the modern baseline pace spread.

options.name: Driver Dominant Era
options.summary: Driver technique shines with a 50% larger cornering/braking impact.
options.description: Grip limits are unpredictable and the cars are a handful, magnifying driver bravery into big lap time swings.

options.name: Precision Assisted Era
options.summary: Advanced stability tools halve the per-point lap time gain to 0.025s.
options.description: Refined chassis feedback and driver aids blunt individual flair, shifting the spotlight onto car development.

options.name: 620 kg Minimum
options.summary: Teams may develop chassis mass down to 620.0 kg, but no lower.
options.description: The rules trim the minimum legal chassis weight to 620.0 kg, opening the door to more aggressive weight reduction.

options.name: 640 kg Minimum
options.summary: The baseline 640.0 kg minimum chassis weight remains in force.
options.description: The governing body keeps the minimum legal chassis weight at 640.0 kg.

options.name: 660 kg Minimum
options.summary: Cars must weigh at least 660.0 kg, forcing heavier chassis into the next season.
options.description: A heavier regulation target raises the minimum legal chassis weight to 660.0 kg.

options.name: Legacy Electronics Ban
options.summary: Traditional bans keep suspension trickery and launch aids illegal.
options.description: The governing body upholds long-standing restrictions on active suspension, traction control, and ABS to preserve driver skill showcases.

options.name: Total Driver Aid Prohibition
options.summary: All electronic driver assists are outlawed across the grid.
options.description: Regulators crack down on every driver assistance system, forcing teams to rely solely on mechanical grip and driver talent.

options.name: Modern Relaxation
options.summary: Electronics arms race allowed; no driver aids are banned.
options.description: The FIA opens the rulebook to innovation, permitting all driver assistance technologies to remain on the cars.

options.name: Active Suspension Clampdown
options.summary: Active suspension remains outlawed while other aids slip through.
options.description: Chassis control systems are singled out as the main threat to spectacle, leaving other electronics untouched.

options.name: Active Aero Restriction
options.summary: Movable aero surfaces are deemed illegal driver assists.
options.description: Variable aero elements are curbed to keep overtaking predictable, though other assistance systems stay in play.

options.name: Traction Control Crackdown
options.summary: Electronics that tame wheelspin are once again outlawed.
options.description: Officials reintroduce a ban on traction control to reward precise throttle modulation from the drivers.

options.name: ABS Clampdown
options.summary: Brake modulation systems are prohibited to keep braking skill central.
options.description: The series pivots back to pure brake feel, eliminating anti-lock software from the cars.

options.name: Thermal Management Limits
options.summary: Advanced TPMS packages are outlawed to spice up tyre wear.
options.description: Stewards curtail tyre telemetry suites, making temperature swings and wear harder to tame.

options.name: Electronics Clampdown
options.summary: Launch and braking aids are removed alongside tyre telemetry.
options.description: A sweeping electronics policy bans the most intrusive driver assists while allowing aero gimmicks to continue.

options.name: Aero & Suspension Split
options.summary: Movable aero and platform tricks are both outlawed this era.
options.description: Regulators focus on mechanical purity, suppressing both active suspension packages and active aero experiments.

options.name: DRS Enabled
options.summary: DRS is available in designated zones from lap 3 onward.
options.description: Overtaking aid remains legal in regulated zones for cars within the activation gap.

options.name: DRS Disabled
options.summary: DRS is banned for all race sessions.
options.description: The governing body removes movable rear-wing assistance, leaving overtakes to slipstream and braking.

options.name: ERS Enabled
options.summary: Standardized battery deployment and harvest systems are legal.
options.description: Cars may use a regulated electrical deployment system that harvests under braking and assists acceleration out of slower zones.

options.name: ERS Disabled
options.summary: No battery deployment is allowed in race sessions.
options.description: The governing body bans electrical deployment, leaving cars to rely on combustion power alone.

options.name: Modern System
options.description: The familiar ten-place scoring table remains in use, rewarding consistency through the field.

options.name: Top 12 Points
options.summary: Extended scoring to 12th place (25 down to 1).
options.description: An expanded table keeps midfield battles meaningful deep into the order.

options.name: Classic Top 8
options.summary: Old-school top 8 scoring (15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1).
options.description: Historic scoring returns, piling pressure on teams to break into the top eight for points.

options.name: 60 Minute Qualifying
options.summary: Single 60-minute session sets the grid.
options.description: All drivers run in one continuous hour, with best laps determining the starting order.

options.name: Knockout Qualifying
options.summary: Three-stage Q1/Q2/Q3 knockout format.
options.description: Drivers are eliminated across Q1 and Q2, with Q3 deciding the top 10 positions.

options.name: Balanced Payout
options.summary: Current balanced payout curve used as the baseline.
options.description: Prize money remains evenly tiered, rewarding both champions and solid midfield outfits.

options.name: Top-Heavy Purse
options.summary: Championship leaders claim the lion's share of the prize pot.
options.description: Broadcasters chase headlines, diverting more revenue to the sharp end of the grid.

options.name: Even Spread
options.summary: Smaller gap between first and last, supporting the whole field.
options.description: Commercial deals insist on stability, smoothing payouts to help backmarkers invest.

options.name: No Testing Limits
options.summary: Teams may run unlimited private test laps, constrained only by budget.
options.description: No restrictions apply to private testing programmes.

options.name: Generous Testing Limits
options.summary: Teams may run up to 1,000 private test laps per season.
options.description: A permissive lap cap keeps costs in check while still allowing meaningful development work.

options.name: Strict Testing Limits
options.summary: Teams may run up to 250 private test laps per season.
options.description: A tight lap cap forces teams to be strategic about private testing.

options.name: Extreme Cap
options.summary: Hard cap of 6 engines and 6 gearboxes per season.
options.description: A strict seasonal allocation rule that forces teams to manage component life very carefully.

options.name: Moderate Cap
options.summary: Cap of 8 engines and 8 gearboxes per season.
options.description: The standard seasonal allocation rule: limited but manageable component pools.

options.name: Generous Cap
options.summary: Cap of 10 engines and 10 gearboxes per season.
options.description: A generous allocation cap that allows more fresh components through the season.

options.name: No Cap
options.summary: No seasonal allocation cap; teams may negotiate any supply.
options.description: Component allocations are not capped by regulations; supply is limited only by budget and supplier constraints.

options.name: No Tyre Allocation Rules
options.summary: Teams may fit a fresh set whenever required.
options.description: Practice, qualifying and races retain the original unlimited fresh-tyre behavior.

options.name: Light Tyre Allocation
options.summary: Each driver receives 15 chosen dry sets for the complete weekend.
options.description: Physical tyre sets retain their wear through practice, qualifying and the race.

options.name: Strict Tyre Allocation
options.summary: Each driver receives only 12 chosen dry sets for the complete weekend.
options.description: Careful practice mileage and qualifying risk management become essential.

options.name: Balanced Compounds
options.summary: Tyre suppliers retain their baseline durability mix.
options.description: The FIA leaves compound construction untouched, keeping tyre wear trends stable.

options.name: Aggressive Compounds
options.summary: All tyre suppliers lose 30 durability rating points across every compound.
options.description: Spicier compounds deliver peak grip at the cost of a heavy, regulation-wide durability hit on every tyre in the range.

options.name: Endurance Focus
options.summary: All tyre suppliers gain 30 durability rating points across every compound.
options.description: Tyre makers prioritise marathon stints, releasing tougher rubber that dramatically improves durability throughout the range.
